To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

people with ASD have a deficit in the processing of a broad range of emotional stimuli, which is present in the auditory and the visual modalities and which cannot be accounted for in terms of a deficit in face processing.
people with ASD have a broad range of impairments in the recognition of basic emotions from faces, body movements and vocal stimuli, and in the ability to make social judgments from facial stimuli.
people with ASD have deficits in the recognition of emotion across a range of modalities and that these deficits are correlated with social judgements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we perceive and understand the emotions of others.
the neural and psychological mechanisms of emotion processing in autism.
the development of new treatments for autism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people with autism spectrum disorder have deficits in facial, body and voice emotion recognition, which are associated with impairments in social judgements.
people with autism have difficulties in recognizing emotions, and that these difficulties are not restricted to the face, or to the visual modality, but extend to body movement and vocal expressions.

the study demonstrates that there is a significant and broad-ranging deficit in emotion processing in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) present across a range a stimulus domains and in auditory and visual modaility; they cannot therefore simply be accounted for in terms of impairements in face processing or the visual modality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people with ASD have deficits in processing emotional information across a range of modalities (faces, body, voice) and this contributes to social difficulties.
there are deficits in emotion processing across a range of social stimuli and modalities in ASD.
there are significant deficits in emotion processing present across a range in the ASD group, and that these are not limited to the visual domain or to the processing of facial expressions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social impairments in people with autism are not restricted to face processing, but are a result of a broad impairment in the recognition of emotion in a wide range of social cues.
the social impairments in autism cannot be attributed to a single deficit in the processing of facial expressions.
people with ASD are not just bad at recognizing emotions from the face, but they have problems with all kinds of social signals.
